mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.5% in a month signals tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as higher borrowing costs reduce corporate investments and consumer spending.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS increases by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a month signals weakening labor market conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where UNRATE rises by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over three months signals weakening consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate lower corporate revenues and earnings.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where RSAFS declines for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals strengthening supply-side conditions, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate higher corporate revenues and earnings.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances where INDPRO increases by more than 1% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) over three months signals easing inflationary pressures, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate a less aggressive monetary policy stance.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL declines for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 300,000 in a month signals a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate higher consumer spending and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances where PAYEMS increases by more than 300,000 in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in housing starts (HOUST) and real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 5% and 1% respectively in a month signals strengthening demand-side conditions, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate higher corporate revenues and earnings.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases > 5% and RSAFS > 1% in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances where HOUST and RSAFS increase by more than 5% and 1% respectively in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 5% for three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as higher borrowing costs reduce corporate investments and consumer spending.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS remains above 5% for three consecutive months.
